paragraphs: AutoManual addresses a practical obstacle for language-model agents: working in a new environment often requires carefully written expert instructions. Instead of relying entirely on that preparation, the framework lets agents develop an instruction manual through interaction. The goal is to turn experience into organized knowledge that supports later decisions.

Two agents maintain this knowledge while interacting with the environment. The Planner writes executable plans using the current rules, and the Builder revises those rules as experience accumulates. A structured rule system supports updates while retaining essential details. The Builder also receives case-conditioned prompts intended to reduce hallucinations during rule management. A separate Formulator then turns the accumulated rules into a readable manual.

With one simple demonstration, the framework reports task success rates of 97.4% with GPT-4-turbo and 86.2% with GPT-3.5-turbo on ALFWorld. These results support the usefulness of learning explicit instructions through interaction. The resulting manual can also guide smaller language models, making the acquired environmental knowledge useful beyond the agent that originally gathered it.
neurips-2024-automanual-constructing-ins.tldr: AutoManual lets language-model agents learn environmental rules through interaction and compile them into readable manuals that improve task planning.

paragraphs: Bench2Drive targets weaknesses in how end-to-end driving systems are compared. Replaying recorded driving logs cannot fully reveal how a model behaves when its own actions affect what happens next. Existing closed-loop evaluations also suffer from variable scores on long routes, while separately collected training data makes algorithm comparisons difficult.

The benchmark provides shared training data and a closed-loop evaluation protocol in CARLA v2. Its training set contains two million annotated frames from 10,000 short clips, covering 44 interactive scenarios, 23 weather conditions, and 12 towns. Scenarios include maneuvers such as overtaking, handling a vehicle cutting in, and taking a detour.

Evaluation spans 220 routes that combine the 44 scenarios with different locations and weather conditions. This structure supports assessment of distinct driving abilities across situations rather than relying solely on an overall long-route score. The authors implement and evaluate leading end-to-end driving models within this setup, providing a common basis for examining their capabilities and identifying directions for improvement.
neurips-2024-bench2drive-towards-multi-a.tldr: Bench2Drive supplies shared training data and 220 closed-loop routes for comparing end-to-end driving systems across distinct interactive abilities.

paragraphs: This paper studies how to estimate outcomes over time under alternative treatments, with particular attention to long-term prediction. Such estimates must account for changing variables that influence both treatment and outcomes. The proposed approach uses recurrent neural networks together with two representation-learning objectives, avoiding the computational expense associated with transformer-based alternatives.

Contrastive Predictive Coding helps the model capture dependencies across time within those changing confounding variables. Information Maximization addresses a separate concern: whether the learned representation retains the information needed for causal identification. The authors argue that overlooking invertible representations can compromise identification assumptions. Their objective maximizes a lower bound on the mutual information between the original sequence and its representation.

The combined method reports state-of-the-art counterfactual estimation on synthetic and real-world data. Its contribution is the pairing of long-term sequence learning with an explicit information-retention objective for causal estimation. The findings support this combination in the reported evaluations; the information objective is presented as a remedy for representation concerns, rather than an unconditional guarantee that causal identification always holds.
neurips-2024-causal-contrastive-learning.tldr: The method combines recurrent networks, contrastive prediction, and information retention to improve long-term counterfactual outcome estimation.

paragraphs: This paper develops a way to certify robustness for Deep Equilibrium Models, a class of implicit neural networks. A robustness certificate establishes a region of input changes within which a prediction is protected. Existing approaches based on interval propagation or Lipschitz bounds give conservative certificates and apply only to particular forms of these models.

The authors first investigate randomized smoothing as a more broadly applicable certification approach. They find that it extends to large-scale datasets, but straightforward application is computationally expensive. Their Serialized Randomized Smoothing method reuses historical information to reduce redundant computation. Because this changes the certification procedure, they also derive a new estimate of the certified radius to establish its theoretical correctness.

Image-recognition experiments and ablation studies report certification speedups of up to seven times, with almost no loss in certified accuracy. The result matters because certification itself can be a substantial computational burden. The contribution therefore combines a more efficient procedure with a matching correctness argument, while the reported speed and accuracy tradeoff remains an empirical finding.
neurips-2024-certified-robustness-for-de.tldr: Serialized Randomized Smoothing reuses prior computation to certify Deep Equilibrium Models up to seven times faster with almost unchanged certified accuracy.

paragraphs: Node embeddings represent the nodes of a network as vectors, allowing ordinary machine-learning methods to work with network structure. They are useful for grouping nodes into communities and predicting connections. Despite their practical success, the abstract identifies a gap in theoretical understanding for common embedding methods beyond spectral clustering.

The paper examines node2vec and the communities obtained by applying k-means to its learned vectors. Its main theorem establishes weakly consistent community recovery for stochastic block models, including degree-corrected versions. In plain terms, the guarantee concerns increasingly reliable recovery under the specified network models, rather than exact recovery for every possible network. The model assumptions are part of the scope of the result.

The authors also discuss using these embeddings for node and link prediction, and present empirical evidence on real and simulated networks. They examine how the findings relate to other network embedding tools. The central contribution is a theoretical foundation for a familiar practical pipeline: learn node2vec representations, then cluster them with k-means.
neurips-2024-community-detection-guarant.tldr: The paper proves weakly consistent community recovery from node2vec embeddings clustered with k-means under specified stochastic block models.

paragraphs: Deep reinforcement-learning methods for robotic control often depend on stored experience or costly updates using batches of samples. Those requirements create difficulties for robots with limited computing resources. The authors show that the methods they examine can fail severely when replay buffers are small or when learning uses only the latest observation.

Their proposed Action Value Gradient method, or AVG, is designed for this incremental setting. Each update uses the most recent sample without a replay buffer or batch update. A set of normalization and scaling techniques addresses the instability that otherwise makes this form of deep policy-gradient learning difficult. The paper also removes reliance on target networks.

On robotic simulation benchmarks, AVG is the only incremental method in the reported comparison that learns effectively, often reaching final performance comparable to batch methods. The authors also demonstrate incremental deep reinforcement learning on a robotic manipulator and a mobile robot. These findings show that useful learning can occur under the paper's much leaner update regime.
neurips-2024-deep-policy-gradient-method.tldr: AVG enables effective deep policy-gradient learning from individual recent samples, with demonstrations in simulation and on two real robotic systems.

paragraphs: This paper focuses on the physical motion underlying string-instrument sound. Although machine learning has made progress in music generation and differentiable sound synthesis, the authors identify less attention to simulations of instrument vibration governed by physical laws. Their target is the motion of nonlinear strings across both space and time.

The proposed neural architecture combines modal synthesis with spectral modeling. It takes mechanical properties and fundamental frequencies as inputs and produces string states at different locations and times. These outputs are intended to solve the partial differential equation describing the nonlinear string. The approach therefore connects the model's inputs and predictions directly to a physical description of the vibrating instrument.

Empirical evaluations find more accurate string-motion simulations than the baseline architectures considered. The stated result concerns how well the model reproduces motion, giving the contribution a concrete physical target within sound-and-motion simulation. The paper's significance is its integration of established synthesis and spectral ideas into a differentiable neural framework for modeling nonlinear vibration.
neurips-2024-differentiable-modal-synthe.tldr: A neural model combining modal synthesis and spectral modeling improves the reported accuracy of physically grounded nonlinear string-motion simulation.

paragraphs: DiffPano addresses text-driven generation of panoramic scenes, including the challenge of keeping different viewpoints consistent. The authors identify three obstacles: limited scene datasets, the complexity of full scenes, and disagreements between separately generated views. Their contribution combines a new training resource with a generation framework designed for panoramas.

The dataset contains millions of consecutive panoramic keyframes accompanied by depth information, camera poses, and text descriptions. Using this resource, the authors adapt Stable Diffusion into a single-view text-to-panorama model through LoRA fine-tuning. They then introduce a multi-view diffusion model that incorporates spherical epipolar relationships to connect panoramic views geometrically.

Experiments show that the framework can generate diverse and consistent panoramas for previously unseen text descriptions and supplied camera poses. The two modeling stages address complementary needs: producing an individual panorama and maintaining agreement across viewpoints. The resulting contribution concerns scalable panoramic scene generation, with the dataset supplying the linked visual, geometric, and language information needed to train that system.
neurips-2024-diffpano-scalable-and-consi.tldr: DiffPano combines a large panoramic dataset with geometry-aware diffusion to generate consistent panoramic views from text and camera poses.

paragraphs: DiTFastAttn tackles the computational cost of attention in diffusion transformers used for image and video generation. Self-attention has quadratic complexity, making it a bottleneck as the amount of visual information grows. The proposed method compresses attention after training by targeting repeated or unnecessarily broad computation during inference.

The authors identify three sources of redundancy. Spatially, many attention heads concentrate on nearby information. Across neighboring diffusion steps, attention outputs can be highly similar. Conditional and unconditional inference also produce similar results in parts of their attention computation. These observations motivate different forms of sharing rather than treating every attention calculation as independent.

Window Attention with Residual Sharing addresses spatial redundancy, Attention Sharing across Timesteps reuses information between generation steps, and Attention Sharing across CFG targets repeated work during conditional generation. Together, the techniques provide a structured approach to reducing attention computation across space, time, and conditioning. The contribution described in the abstract is this post-training compression design, grounded in the three observed similarities.
neurips-2024-ditfastattn-attention-compr.tldr: DiTFastAttn compresses diffusion-transformer attention by sharing computation across spatial regions, neighboring steps, and conditional generation paths.

paragraphs: FedMEKI is a benchmark for incorporating medical knowledge into foundation models when data cannot simply be collected in one place. It uses cross-silo federated learning, organizing training across separate data holders. This addresses the centralization difficulties that arise when medical information is subject to privacy constraints.

The platform covers multiple sites, data types, and tasks. Its seven modalities include images, signals, text, laboratory results, vital signs, and input and output variables. The curated data supports six classification tasks and two generation tasks, spanning activities such as detecting lung opacity, predicting mortality, answering medical visual questions, and clarifying noisy ECG signals. Data is partitioned among clients for decentralized training.

The benchmark includes 16 approaches, creating a shared setting for studying how medical knowledge can be incorporated across this varied collection. The authors present FedMEKI as enabling foundation models to learn from a broader range of medical information without directly exposing the underlying data. Its central value is bringing privacy-constrained, multi-modal medical learning into a common evaluation framework.
neurips-2024-fedmeki-a-benchmark-for-sca.tldr: FedMEKI benchmarks federated medical foundation-model adaptation across seven data modalities, eight tasks, and 16 approaches.

paragraphs: FINALLY targets speech recordings degraded by background noise, reverberation, and microphone artifacts. The paper revisits generative adversarial networks for restoring clear speech. Its theoretical analysis argues that these networks tend toward the highest-density point in the clean-speech distribution conditioned on the recording, a behavior the authors consider valuable for enhancement.

The work also studies how perceptual losses can stabilize adversarial training. Such losses compare representations of audio, making the choice of feature extractor consequential. The authors develop a way to probe feature-space structure and use the results to select a WavLM-based perceptual loss. They combine it with an adversarial training pipeline based on multi-scale short-time Fourier transforms.

The resulting model extends the HiFi++ architecture with a WavLM encoder and the new training procedure. Across several datasets, the authors report high-quality speech at 48 kHz and state-of-the-art enhancement performance. The contribution connects a theoretical motivation for adversarial learning with a concrete representation and training design that works well in the reported evaluations.
neurips-2024-finally-fast-and-universal-.tldr: FINALLY combines adversarial training and WavLM-based perceptual guidance to achieve reported state-of-the-art speech enhancement at 48 kHz.

paragraphs: GTSinger is a singing dataset designed to support controllable and personalized singing systems. The authors identify shortcomings in existing resources, including limited language and singer diversity, weak recording quality, and missing information about technique and musical scores. Their contribution combines recordings with detailed annotations and task benchmarks.

The corpus contains 80.59 hours of singing from 20 professional singers across nine languages. Six singing techniques have phoneme-level annotations and controlled comparisons, supporting work on recognizing and controlling how a phrase is sung. Realistic music scores, manually aligned phonemes, and global style labels connect the recordings to musical structure and expressive choices. The dataset also includes 16.16 hours of paired speech.

Four benchmark experiments demonstrate intended uses: technique-controlled synthesis, technique recognition, style transfer, and speech-to-singing conversion. These tasks draw on different parts of the same annotated resource. The paper's main contribution is therefore a shared, free-to-use foundation for studying several singing capabilities, with paired information that connects vocal content, technique, style, and speech.
neurips-2024-gtsinger-a-global-multi-tec.tldr: GTSinger provides multilingual professional singing, detailed technique annotations, realistic scores, and benchmarks for four singing tasks.

paragraphs: Sparse autoencoders try to explain language-model activations using a small number of learned features. This can make internal activity easier to interpret, but the penalty used to encourage sparsity also distorts feature strengths. In particular, it can cause shrinkage: active features are assigned systematically smaller values than they should receive.

The Gated Sparse Autoencoder separates deciding which features are active from estimating how strongly they are active. It applies the sparsity penalty only to the selection component. This division limits the penalty's unwanted influence on magnitude estimation while preserving pressure to explain activations with relatively few features.

In experiments on language models with up to seven billion parameters, the authors find that Gated SAEs eliminate shrinkage within typical hyperparameter ranges and remain similarly interpretable. They also achieve comparable reconstruction quality with half as many active features. This reported improvement means a more compact explanation can retain similar fidelity, improving the tradeoff between sparsity and reconstruction without an observed loss of interpretability.
neurips-2024-improving-sparse-decomposit.tldr: Gated sparse autoencoders separate feature selection from strength estimation, achieving comparable reconstructions with half as many active features in the reported experiments.

paragraphs: KVQuant addresses the memory consumed by cached key and value activations when language models process long contexts. Compressing this cache could support much longer inputs, but representing its values with fewer than four bits is difficult without losing accuracy. The method adapts quantization to the structure of these activations.

It quantizes keys by channel and before rotary positional embeddings, uses non-uniform representations tailored to each layer's sensitivity, and separates unusually large values within each vector. These choices address different sources of quantization error: mismatched grouping, positional transformations, uneven value distributions, and outliers that distort the range used for compression.

Across the listed LLaMA-family and Mistral models, three-bit quantization produces less than 0.1 perplexity degradation on Wikitext-2 and C4. The method enables serving LLaMA-7B with up to one million context tokens on one A100-80GB GPU and ten million on eight GPUs. Custom kernels also achieve up to approximately 1.7-fold speedups over baseline fp16 matrix-vector multiplication for LLaMA-7B.
neurips-2024-kvquant-towards-10-million-.tldr: KVQuant compresses language-model KV caches to three bits with small reported perplexity changes, enabling substantially longer contexts on specified GPU systems.

paragraphs: Learning from Teaching, or LoT, is a regularization method intended to help neural networks generalize beyond their training data. Its starting hypothesis is that useful, generalizable relationships should be relatively easy for another learner to imitate. This turns teachability into a possible signal for improving the model being trained.

The method introduces auxiliary student learners that learn from the main model. Their learning then provides feedback to that model, encouraging it to capture relationships that are both imitable and generalizable. Teaching is therefore part of the main model's training process, with students serving as a source of feedback about the information it has learned.

Experiments in computer vision, natural language processing, and reinforcement learning report significant benefits over training on the original dataset alone. The authors interpret the results as evidence that LoT can retain useful information at appropriate scales while discarding spurious correlations. The findings support the approach across the tested settings, while the connection between ease of imitation and generalization remains the method's motivating hypothesis.
neurips-2024-learning-from-teaching-regu.tldr: LoT uses feedback from auxiliary students to encourage a main model to learn relationships that are easier to imitate and generalize.

paragraphs: LLaNA explores whether a language assistant can understand objects directly from a Neural Radiance Field, or NeRF. A NeRF stores information about an object's geometry and visual appearance in neural-network weights. The paper treats those weights as an input modality for language-based understanding, including captioning and answering questions.

The assistant extracts information directly from the weights of the NeRF's multilayer perceptron. It therefore does not need to first render images or construct explicit 3D representations. This is the central design choice: the learned representation of the object becomes the material the assistant reads when producing descriptions or answers.

The authors also construct a dataset of NeRFs paired with text annotations without human intervention and develop a benchmark from it. On this benchmark, directly processing NeRF weights compares favorably with extracting 2D or 3D representations from the same NeRFs. The findings support the feasibility of using neural scene representations themselves as a source of information for multimodal language assistants.
neurips-2024-llana-large-language-and-ne.tldr: LLaNA captions and answers questions about NeRF-encoded objects by reading network weights directly, with favorable results on a newly constructed benchmark.

paragraphs: This paper examines whether methods for adapting closed language models actually protect sensitive data while delivering competitive performance. It evaluates four recent approaches, considering their threat models, different differential-privacy levels, multiple model architectures, and datasets for classification and generation. The comparison also includes three private gradient-based adaptation methods for locally run open models.

The authors find that all four closed-model approaches expose inference-time query data to the provider. Three also expose large portions of private training data. The remaining approach protects training data but requires a local open language model. These distinctions matter because protecting training examples does not by itself protect the sensitive information users submit later.

In the reported comparisons, all four approaches perform worse and incur higher training and query costs than the local open-model alternatives. The authors consequently recommend open models for private adaptation given the methods and models studied. That conclusion is explicitly tied to the available approaches examined, rather than establishing that every possible future closed-model adaptation must share these weaknesses.
neurips-2024-open-llms-are-necessary-for.tldr: An evaluation of four closed-model private adaptation methods finds privacy exposure, lower performance, and higher costs than tested local open-model alternatives.

paragraphs: Learning physical motion from data is difficult because predictions must reflect the structure of the underlying system. Energy-conservation priors can help, but many real systems do not conserve energy. This paper proposes a regularization term based on time-reversal symmetry and investigates why it can help beyond systems that physically possess that symmetry.

The term supports energy preservation in conservative systems and provides an inductive bias for reversible, non-conservative systems. The authors also give a numerical argument for broader usefulness: they prove that the time-reversal loss can improve modeling accuracy by minimizing higher-order Taylor terms in ordinary differential equation integration. This connects the loss to numerical accuracy even for irreversible systems.

The proposed model, TREAT, incorporates the loss into neural ordinary differential equations. Experiments across diverse physical systems report superior performance, including an 11.5% mean-squared-error improvement for a chaotic triple pendulum. The contribution is both a practical regularizer and an explanation of how a physically motivated constraint can provide numerical benefits outside its original physical setting.
neurips-2024-physics-informed-regulariza.tldr: TREAT uses time-reversal regularization to improve neural dynamical models, supported by a numerical analysis and experiments across varied physical systems.

paragraphs: Non-exemplar class-incremental learning asks a model to recognize new categories while retaining old ones without storing old training examples. This makes conflicts between old and new categories difficult to resolve after they appear. Prospective Representation Learning addresses that difficulty by preparing the representation space before future classes arrive.

During initial training, the method compresses the distribution of current class embeddings to leave room for later categories. During incremental learning, it pushes new-class features away from stored prototypes of old classes in a latent space. It also aligns the model's current embedding space with that latent space as the model changes, helping new classes occupy the reserved regions.

The intended effect is to reduce disruption to previously learned categories while making room for new ones. The method can be added to existing non-exemplar incremental-learning baselines, and experiments on several benchmarks report performance beyond the compared state-of-the-art methods. The contribution is a forward-looking organization of representations that complements the later task of balancing old and new classes.
neurips-2024-prospective-representation-.tldr: Prospective Representation Learning reserves embedding space for future categories to improve class-incremental learning without retaining old examples.

paragraphs: Slot-VLM studies how to turn a video's dense visual features into a useful input for a language model. A video contains both detailed objects and changes over time, and these call for different sampling choices. The framework summarizes these complementary kinds of information through representative tokens called object and event slots.

Its Object-Event Slots module has two branches. The object branch uses high spatial resolution with fewer sampled frames, emphasizing the appearance and details of objects. The event branch uses more frequent frames at lower spatial resolution, emphasizing temporal dynamics. Each branch adaptively aggregates the vision encoder's dense tokens into a smaller set of meaningful representations.

The two sets of slots are combined into the visual context supplied to the language model for reasoning. Experiments report state-of-the-art video question-answering performance. The approach matters because it gives object detail and temporal change distinct routes into the final representation, allowing the language model to receive both kinds of evidence when answering questions about a video.
neurips-2024-slot-vlm-object-event-slots.tldr: Slot-VLM summarizes detailed objects and temporal events through complementary token sets, achieving reported state-of-the-art video question answering.

paragraphs: SpelsNet divides 3D point clouds into surface elements using information from the boundary representations common in computer-aided design. The problem involves both spatial shape and topology: which elements belong together and how they connect. The proposed system learns from these two sources of structure jointly.

The authors introduce a point-to-BRep adjacency representation that brings the graph structure of a boundary representation into the point-cloud setting. SpelsNet then uses two components. A supervised spatial segmentation head predicts element types and point memberships, while a graph-based head uses the topological supervision. Together, they are designed to produce segmentation that is accurate and consistent with the underlying connections.

To support this training setup, the authors add the necessary annotations to two existing CAD datasets. Experiments on those datasets show the effectiveness of SpelsNet and its topological supervision compared with the selected baselines and state-of-the-art approaches. The contribution is therefore both an architecture and a representation that makes CAD connectivity available as a learning signal for point-cloud segmentation.
neurips-2024-spelsnet-surface-primitive-.tldr: SpelsNet combines spatial segmentation with boundary-representation graph supervision to identify topologically consistent surface elements in 3D point clouds.

paragraphs: Sequential Monte Carlo Policy Optimisation, or SPO, combines planning with reinforcement learning. The paper targets a scaling difficulty in approaches that use tree search and self-play: much of their search proceeds sequentially. Engineering workarounds can improve practical execution, but the authors note that these can also reduce performance.

SPO is a model-based reinforcement-learning algorithm developed within the Expectation Maximisation framework. It uses sample-based search, which applies to both discrete and continuous action spaces without changing the algorithm. The authors show robust policy improvement and emphasize that the search can run in parallel, making it suitable for hardware accelerators.

Experiments report statistically significant performance improvements over both model-free and model-based baselines across continuous and discrete environments. The parallel search also exhibits favorable scaling behavior. These results connect the algorithm's planning design to two practical outcomes: stronger performance in the evaluated tasks and effective use of additional computing resources. Its shared treatment of different action spaces broadens the settings in which the same method can be applied.
neurips-2024-spo-sequential-monte-carlo-.tldr: SPO uses parallel sample-based planning to improve reinforcement-learning policies across discrete and continuous tasks while scaling effectively on accelerators.

paragraphs: This paper investigates how transformers can use examples in a prompt to perform a task without changing their parameters. It approaches this in-context learning behavior through representation learning, asking whether the computation performed by attention can be understood as a form of learning in a related model.

Using kernel methods, the authors derive a dual model for a single softmax attention layer. The attention layer's inference corresponds to training this dual model, and its token-representation predictions match the dual model's test outputs. This equivalence provides a mathematical way to study an inference-time process through the training behavior of another model.

The analysis yields a generalization-error bound related to the number of demonstration tokens. The authors extend their conclusions to a full transformer layer and multiple attention layers, and propose potential attention modifications inspired especially by contrastive learning. Experiments support their findings. The contribution offers a representation-learning explanation for the analyzed computations, while treating the broader mechanism of in-context learning as an ongoing question.
neurips-2024-towards-understanding-how-t.tldr: The paper links attention-based in-context learning to training a dual representation model and derives a bound involving demonstration-token quantity.

paragraphs: LexVLA aims to make image-text alignment easier to interpret. Instead of comparing representations whose dimensions have unclear meanings, it represents each input through its similarities to vocabulary words. This gives the representation a lexical meaning, so individual word matches can help explain how images and text align.

Learning these representations is difficult without direct supervision and can produce meaningless word activations. LexVLA combines DINOv2's visual features with Llama 2's ability to predict lexical content in context. An overuse penalty discourages words from activating frequently without useful meaning. The two pretrained models are aligned through multimodal fine-tuning without an intricate training setup.

On cross-modal retrieval benchmarks, LexVLA trained on CC-12M outperforms the compared models fine-tuned on larger datasets and models trained from scratch on much larger collections. This finding supports the combination of lexical interpretability and competitive retrieval performance in the evaluated setting. The result also highlights how pretrained single-modality models can be brought into a shared word-based representation through multimodal alignment.
neurips-2024-unified-lexical-representat.tldr: LexVLA aligns images and text through interpretable vocabulary-based representations and outperforms larger-data comparators on reported retrieval benchmarks.

paragraphs: VASA-1 generates a talking-face video from one still image and a speech recording. Its goal extends beyond matching mouth movements to sound: it also produces facial expressions and head motion that make the resulting face appear more natural and lively. These behaviors are generated together as part of the facial dynamics.

The system uses a diffusion model operating in a learned face latent space, a representation of facial information. The authors develop this space from videos so that it is expressive and disentangled, supporting the modeling of facial movement and head motion. This representation and the holistic movement-generation model are the central technical contributions.

Experiments, including newly introduced evaluation metrics, report substantial improvements over prior methods across several dimensions. The model supports online generation of 512-by-512 video at up to 40 frames per second with negligible starting latency. These findings combine visual quality with responsiveness, supporting the possibility of real-time avatar interactions that reproduce aspects of human conversational facial behavior.
neurips-2024-vasa-1-lifelike-audio-drive.tldr: VASA-1 turns a still face and speech audio into expressive talking video, supporting 512-by-512 generation at up to 40 frames per second.
